newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN REJECTS ALL BIDS IN T-BILL AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN REJECTS ALL BIDS IN T-BILL AUCTION.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Wednesday rejected all 150 million crowns worth of bids in an auction of four-week treasury bills, the central bank (NBS) said in a statement.
The statement did not give any further details but a senior finance ministry official said the bids were rejected because banks demanded too high yields.

"They (banks) submitted bids with demanded yield between 60 to 90 percent and that is simply unacceptable," Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters.
Horvath said the state budget reckoned with rate costs for refinancing the budget deficit at only around 10 percent on local state securities operations.
Average yield in the last successful auction of four-week T-bills hit 14.21 percent on May 7, up from 13.277 percent in the previous successful auction of similar paper on March 13.
The high levels of yields demanded arose because of an accute liquidity shortage on the local money market brought about by the central bank's battle to defend the crown.

Earlier on Wednesday, the average yield in a central bank overnight repo tender hit 54.56 percent and some Slovak banks were reported to have bought short-term crown funds for over 100 percent on the money market.

Horvath said the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has several times this year helped to refinance the state budget deficit by buying T-bills. By law, the NBS may hold state securities totalling to up to eight percent of overall 1996 budget revenues.

The ministry uses T-bills and state bonds as the main tools to cover the state budget deficit, which totalled 3.45 billion crowns in the first quarter of 1997, up from a shortfall of 361.3 million crowns for the first two months of this year.
